title: FQP: A Fibonacci Quantization Processor with Multiplication-Free Computing and Topological-Order Routing
problem: Neural networks with escalating parameter sizes require excessive computational power and memory access. Conventional low bit-width uniform quantization causes accuracy degradation due to mismatch between quantization scheme and actual weight/activation data distributions.
motivation: As neural networks scale in size, efficient low bit-width quantization is critical to reduce computational and memory demands without sacrificing accuracy.
method: FQP proposes Fibonacci-based non-uniform quantization to better match neural network data distributions. The processor eliminates expensive multiplication operations through multiplication-free computing techniques. Topological-order routing optimizes data flow and reduces memory access overhead in the hardware architecture.
key_novelty: Using Fibonacci quantization instead of uniform quantization to adapt to actual weight and activation distributions while implementing multiplication-free computing.
contributions: Fibonacci quantization scheme for low bit-width neural networks with improved distribution matching
Multiplication-free processor architecture to reduce computational complexity and power
Topological-order routing for efficient data movement and reduced memory bandwidth
Complete FQP hardware accelerator design for quantized neural network inference
limitations: Limitations and experimental comparisons not discussed in provided abstract.
primary_theme: Fibonacci quantization processor for efficient neural network inference
